title: Go Off, Sis: Jenee Naylor of HighLowLuxxe on Making a Plan and Letting Go of Perfection
text:
Go Off, Sis: Jenee Naylor of HighLowLuxxe on Making a Plan and Letting Go of Perfection

For Jenee Naylor, success requires a roadmap. Now, that doesn’t mean following a traditional path or climbing the corporate ladder, but rather looking to others for what is possible. ‘Seeing is believing,’ the founder of 12PM Studios tells host Erica Chidi Cohen, and now she hopes to inspire other Black women by sharing all that she’s learned. 

Before Jenee made her first major splash with her blog HighLowLuxxe, she got her start on the floor of a Target store in the DMV. She started managing a team of people and moving up the ranks. “I learned how to be a business person through that role,” she shares. She thrived in leadership, particularly because it allowed her to pour into others; she loved teaching, training, and getting people promoted; she was a campus recruiter for Howard. In many ways, it laid the foundation for what was to come. Working for a big store taught her the value of strategy and everything having a place.  “So much of my personality is about being efficient and making the most of things.” 

Her blog, HighLowLuxxe, was “something clever that represented me,” Jenee says it was true to who she was at the time, mostly shopping fast fashion but splurging on something with her bonus check. It was the perfect blend of Jenee’s expertise and her sharing what she was learning about the world of luxury. Part of what made the blog such a success was Jenee’s honest approach to creating content. Sure, she’d have a flawless beat, but she’d shoot her videos in one take. And authenticity might be the key to her long-term success. “Consistency and longevity are hard to maintain if you are putting on an act,” she shares. 

It takes a lot of bravery to walk away from something when it’s working, and working well. Although HighLowLuxxe was a resounding success, Jenee felt called to build something in her own name. She

walked away from high/low luxe to build 12PM Studios, her extremely chic sunglasses company. Why eyewear? For one, it’s “the only thing I care enough about to talk about every day,” Jenee laughs. But also, once Jenee reached the point of success where others were photographing her, she realized sunglasses can offer a bit of protection, a very chic shield from the outside world. So, she looked at what was out there, how others were succeeding, trusted her instincts, and built herself another roadmap. Learn more about how she got from managing a Target to selling her products in Target in this episode of Go Off, Sis.

title: It’s The Summer Of Chunky Jewelry Maxxing
text:
It’s The Summer Of Chunky Jewelry Maxxing

This summer’s biggest trend, quite literally, is chunky jewelry. Unlike most seasonal trends, this one is not going anywhere anytime soon. Once you fall for chunky jewelry, it quietly becomes part of your personal style, to the point where people can’t imagine you without it.

No one embraced the spirit of chunky jewelry quite like the late, great fashion icon Iris Apfel. Long before oversized bangles and sculptural necklaces took over the fashion world, she built an unforgettable personal style around maximalist jewelry. Her bold accessories became a reflection of her fearless personality, making it almost impossible to picture her without them. And from what we’re seeing now, maybe we’re all channeling our inner Iris Apfel this summer.

Whether it’s a beach day, a city stroll, dinner plans, or a night out, chunky jewelry belongs everywhere. After all, an accessory is the finishing touch that can completely transform any outfit.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Bella 🦋 (@bellahadid)

Although the chunky jewelry trend can be traced back to the 2010s, fashion has been moving in this direction again over the past few years. Schiaparelli was among the first to bring statement jewelry back into the spotlight in 2023 with its surrealist accessories. And as maximalism gradually made its way from the runway into everyday wardrobes, surrealist jewelry evolved into something far more wearable.

This change became even more visible on the latest runways, with Sarah Burton’s debut Givenchy SS26 collection showcasing oversized necklaces and statement earrings, while Zimmermann’s SS26 collection featured sculptural jewelry alongside its romantic summer aesthetic.

This summer, the bigger the better. Less layering of dainty pieces, and more styling with larger accessories. Sometimes, all it takes is one great find to become the centerpiece of your wardrobe. My go-to summer outfit formula starts with a white tank top, relaxed linen trousers, oversized sunglasses, kitten heel mules, and as much chunky jewelry as I can get. Colorful resin bangles, sculptural earrings, and playful shapes always work together. The only rule I stick to is keeping each jewelry category consistent: silver with silver, resin with resin. Another key element is to let just one jewelry category do the talking.

During the day, style a sheer cape top with denim shorts, flip-flops, and oversized resin bangles for an effortless summer look. For evenings, pair a simple midi summer dress with sculptural gold earrings, chunky gold rings, and strappy heels. For me, everything else in your outfit can change, but a great chunky ring stack can remain your signature finishing touch. The trick is this: chunky rings are the ultimate day-to-night jewelry, and, sometimes, even piece you’ll wear for a lifetime, like Dua Lipa’s chunky engagement ring, which has quickly become one of the most talked-about jewelry pieces of the year.

In the summer, chunky jewelry can take the form of an abstract shape, like fruit, flowers, or seashells. Pair oversized shell earrings with a monochrome matching set for an effortless vacation look, or let a stack of colorful resin bangles elevate a simple white sundress. One of my personal favorites in my jewelry drawer is a pair of oversized cherry earrings, which I happily wear with everything from a white tank and denim shorts to a simple midi dress. Whichever way you choose to style it, chunky jewelry is the perfect trend to express yourself and be as loud as you want, like Apfel proudly did. 

And when fall arrives, Valentino’s FW26 collection proves that oversized jewelry also works just as well layered over knitwear and tailored coats. You can also layer thick bracelets over fitted long-sleeve tops and style oversized chokers over turtlenecks. Voilà, you’re ready to take this “summer” trend into the cooler months.

title: Nicolandria Is (Reportedly) Over. Why Do We Care So Much About Celebrity Breakups?
text:
Nicolandria Is (Reportedly) Over. Why Do We Care So Much About Celebrity Breakups?

Love is dead. Or so it feels for many fans after celebrity couples announce their breakups. Love Island Season 7 stars Olandria Carthen and Nic Vansteenberghe have broken up after a year of dating, PEOPLE exclusively reports. The popular couple “decided to part ways” as, the PEOPLE source claims, “the distance between them and their busy schedules made it challenging to maintain their connection.” The source continues: “They still remain close friends. They share a deep love and respect for each other and will always support one another whenever possible.”

2026 has also ushered in other high profile celebrity breakups, like Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff (a Qualley source told PEOPLE that the couple is “figuring things out” amid the split), Ariana Grande and Ethan Slater (she has since reconnected with her ex, Ricky Alvarez), Sue Bird and Megan Rapinoe (lesbians around the world were devastated) and Megan Thee Stallion and Klay Thompson, just to name a few. Each of these breakups made headlines (for various reasons) and caused our timelines to speculate, rage, mourn, or all three. It’s natural to be upset when a couple you think you know — or one you were simply rooting hard for — breaks up. When it comes to Nic and Olandria, they have a very specific microscope on their relationship, and the amount of parasocial obsession with their love story seemed to reach heights the internet had never seen. There are the “contract is up!” people who think they were never really dating in the first place, the “love is dead!” camp who pinned all their romantic hopes on the duo, and the “I don’t believe it” folks who are living in denial that PEOPLE magazine is a celeb-friendly source often used by publicists as an unofficial “official” way to get news to the public. It’s safe to say that Nicolandria is done. What’s clear for sure is that everyone has an opinion, and people really care about celebrity breakups.

In 2023, after the breakup of Joe Manganiello and Sofia Vergara, Alicia Vrajlal wrote for Refinery29 that, “Admittedly, I’m one of [the people who mourn celeb breakups]. Like many fans, I was devastated when I heard the news and overwhelmed with a sense of sorrow and disbelief. It can’t be true. Everything seemed to be going so well. I almost wanted to cry. “

But in a world where Hollywood splits are so common, and celebrity worship is becoming at once more intense than ever and more scrutinized, why do we care so much about the relationship breakdowns of famous people we’ve never met?

‘Relationship goals’ is a term often thrown around when it comes to celebrities, because they tend to publicly portray the ideal or fantasy of what a relationship looks like or can aspire to be. But our understanding of #RelationshipGoals has shifted. In 2021, we wrote that, “Not only do #RelationshipGoals fetishize an image that’s curated and not real, they also glorify a type of love that prioritizes staying together (aka building a brand) over anything else.” When we look at stars and project them to be attractive yet down-to-earth, and have busy careers but still find time for dates and cute grocery trips together, we are inadvertently creating the idea that their romance can survive the odds, no matter what. In reality, everything ends, and we don’t know these people. That said, it’s natural to be curious and to care.

“Many of us are interested in celebrities and other public figures and are naturally curious about their lives,” psychologist Dr Marny Lishman tells Refinery29. “At some level, their lives are so unattainable and almost fantasy-like to us, but at another level, many of the same trials and tribulations they endure are not unlike our own.”

It’s because of this that we live vicariously through them when we’re single, and unconsciously strive for the relationship success they have when we’re in a relationship of our own. With that being said, it only makes sense that when a celebrity couple calls it quits, we too feel a sudden loss. We are worried about the Nicolandria hive.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Ericka Hart, M.Ed. (@ihartericka)

In 2023, Nina, 23, said she felt this loss when Lisa Bonet and Jason Momoa broke up in January 2022. At the time, when Phoebe Bridgers and Paul Mescal (who is now dating Gracie Abrams) called time on their romance, Nina was also shook.

“While I definitely don’t get upset about all the famous breakups, these ones truly made me sad,” she tells Refinery29, explaining she was inspired by certain aspects of each couple’s relationships.

“When couples you look up to split up, it kind of gives you a ‘romance and love are dead’ feeling, which sucks. They gave the impression that even relationships with barriers — age differences, dealing with so much fame and gossip or personal drama — stood a chance.”

Lishman explains that we’re often only exposed to one version of reality when it comes to celebrity relationships. This makes our disbelief that much stronger when the romances collapse.

“We idolize their relationships too as we idolize the celebrity, so when the ‘seemingly perfect’ relationship ends, we grieve for the ending of what we perceived as perfection,” says Lishman.

“We see a fairly edited version of reality, so it’s hard to understand why a seemingly perfect relationship would end. At times we are shocked because it ‘looked’ so good.”

Nina agrees, saying that she has “put celebrity couples on a pedestal” in the past, looking to them for “inspiration and confirmation of romance in the world.” So when it all comes crumbling down, it’s a bit of a reality check.

“When they break up, it’s just a sad reminder that no one is immune to the realities and difficulties of love and commitment,” she says.

Lishman explains that this realization is very normal. While it’s hard for many of us to process the news when a seemingly perfect celeb couple breaks up, we know that to some degree (without the fame and fortune), they are just like us.

“They are complex, imperfect creatures that go through highs and lows in life, just like we do. They lose love, they break up, they grieve, they get rejected — just like the rest of us.”

Social media has only exacerbated our passionate responses to celebrity splits. In a time when we watch so many celebrities carefully curate their TikToks with ‘relatable’ couple vids, or flirt up a storm in the comments section, how can we not get deeply invested in their blossoming romances?

“Social media allows us to connect more with them [celebrities], and also be more informed about what’s going in their lives. It gives us more information than traditional media, so we seem to be more invested,” says Lishman.

We’re also seeing more celebrities who find love on a reality TV dating shows (like Nic and Olandria) or on the set of a film, which makes us feel like we’ve been on the journey with them — from the first date to the breakup announcement post on Instagram. And in some cases (like Love Island couples), we actually have. No matter how hard you felt it when High School Musical stars Zac Efron and Vanessa Hudgens split in 2010, we weren’t privy to watching their entire love story play out on camera. Sure, we watched the young love blossom from HSM 1 to 3, and it’s hard not to recall their affection and red carpet cuteness fondly, it’s a whole different beast when a couple’s first kiss and every flirtation is caught on camera. That’s why we’re in the depths of people being extremely not normal about celebrity breakups (just look at how some Swifties still talk about Joe Alwyn). For the celebs, navigating the public scrutiny also seems to be tougher than ever.

Olandria just had to clap back at unverified gossip platform, DeuxMoi, for circulating a rumor that she’s been hooking up with Travis Scott. Olandria denied this claim and commented, “I hope you have your lawyers ready bc I have mine.” According to Cosmo, Olandria’s comment has been deleted or hidden from the public. DeuxMoi confirmed in a pinned comment, “Update: Olandria denied(?) this rumor but blocked this account so her comment, which was pinned was not showing it was from her.”

As the likes of Nic, Olandria, and other celebs, continue to navigate their respective breakups, there will always be fans who are still rooting for them, who will shamelessly keep caring about their favorite celebrity couples (and their breakups), in the hope that there will be just as many moments filled with joy as there will be grief. Some of these people need to go outside and touch grass, while others (like us!) are invested in healthy, completely normal ways. (It’s a good thing Tom Holland and Zendaya are going to stay together forever, right? Right!?) These are people’s real lives, but often it can feel like we’re still watching a fictional love story play out, or that the stakes are just who’s coupled up in a villa. That’s why you see so many people unable to let go of their fave celeb couples — for better and for worse.

After all, how many of us have secretly harbored the hope that Jennifer Lopez and Ben Affleck will rekindle their flame one day (again!)? For some couples, a breakup is certainly the right decision. But as fans, it’s easy to hope that some of our favorite couples will get back together (again, think Bennifer 2.0, or Justin and Hailey Bieber or OTP Tom and Zendaya). Regardless of whether the split is temporary or permanent, we just need to remember that hope is not dead, and neither is love.

This article referencing celebrity breakups was originally published, in part, in 2023. It has since been updated to include recent celeb relationship news.

title: Bikini Tops Are the New Going-Out Top: Here’s How To Style Them
text:
Bikini Tops Are the New Going-Out Top: Here’s How To Style Them

A heatwave? No problem. As temperatures continue to rise, bikini tops are no longer just beachwear; they’ve become a practical and stylish solution for summer style, whether you’re on vacation or in the city. This is the trend we’ve all been waiting for, because your bikini top definitely deserves a chance beyond the pool side this summer.

There’s just something about an outfit that feels slightly unfinished that perfectly captures the carefree spirit of summer and gives me a real sense of freedom. Even when I’m not on holiday, summer itself inspires me to be more creative with the way I dress.

This season, the bikini top has evolved from being that “just in case” item tossed into your vacation suitcase to becoming one of the go-to tops for grabbing a coffee, stopping by the market on the weekend, or heading out for dinner. Thanks especially to Dua Lipa’s summer wardrobe, the line between swimwear and citywear feels more blurred than ever this season.

There are countless ways to style your bikini top, but with the rising temperatures and ever-changing trends, it can be more confusing than ever to know where to start. Need some styling tips? There are a few celebrity-approved ways to wear the trend. From Kylie Jenner’s latest bikini rotation and Gigi Hadid‘s effortless off-duty style to the festival style inspired by Charli XCX’s Brat era, your starting point for making this trend your own is ahead. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Hailey Rhode Bieber (@haileybieber)

Swimwear design is also starting to shift in parallel with this trend. Rather than relying on traditional swimwear prints and beach-inspired aesthetics, recent collections are increasingly drawing inspiration from everyday city life.

For example, in the recent KHY x Frankies Bikinis collaboration, founder Francesca Aiello told WWD that the collection was inspired by her shared love of Los Angeles with Kylie Jenner, hoping that it “felt as unique and sexy as the city itself.” So, rather than looking to the beach as its primary source of inspiration, the collection looks to the city’s aesthetic for a modern approach.

How To Style Bikini Tops

And just like that, this summer’s unofficial “holy trinity” has practically formed itself: a timeless bikini top, comfortable flip-flops you can walk all day in, and a hand fan you’re never willing to put down. Suddenly, getting dressed during a heatwave feels much less complicated. My favorite styling trick is letting colorful bikini details and string straps peek out from under a tiny white tank top and barrel-leg trousers. 

Throw a lightweight linen shirt over your shoulders or tie it around your waist, then accessorize with chunky gold earrings, layered necklaces, and a tote bag. Just a few touches make the outfit feel intentional rather than accidental, turning the bikini top into a natural part of your everyday summer wardrobe.

If you’re spending your sunny days in the city rather than on vacation, take inspiration from Dua Lipa’s effortless vacation aesthetic by pairing a black triangle bikini top with relaxed denim shorts, a lightweight oversized jacket, and simple strappy sandals. Boldly colored bikinis with relaxed jeans also simply give an instant cool-girl feel.

For a summer night out, you can swap the shorts for fun pants, adding a metallic bikini top, black sunglasses, and kitten mules. The look is instantly evening-ready, making it a great choice for a club or festival.

My personal favorite is wearing a polka-dot bikini top over a white baby tee with a midi skirt, flip-flops, and a mini handbag. The fun part of this trend is that there are no rules; it’s just an experiment with different silhouettes, colors, prints, and accessories until you find your own style.

title: Belmont Cameli’s Hair Routine Is Surprisingly Low Maintenance, Thanks To These 3 Products
text:
Belmont Cameli’s Hair Routine Is Surprisingly Low Maintenance, Thanks To These 3 Products

Actor Belmont Cameli might be known for his sweet smile, adorable dance moves, and yes, a sculpted six-pack — but I’d argue his signature curls are the real scene-stealers. So much so, in fact, that his tousled ringlets caught the attention of TRESemmé, which tapped Cameli as the newest face (and, of course, hair) of its Bouncy Curls range.

“I was super excited to be involved,” Cameli tells Refinery29, “and once I got ahold of the products, I quickly learned how simple they are to use. “The products all work really well together, and it’s a pretty light-lift routine.” 

Though Cameli is fully in his curly-hair era now, he didn’t always embrace his natural texture. “My hair has evolved quite a bit,” he says. “It was poker straight when I was a kid, and then in middle school I had the Justin Bieber swoop — I kept a brush and a mirror in my locker.” By high school, though, his curls had taken on a life of their own. “My hair started getting wavy and then curly, and now it just keeps getting curlier, which I love.”

Ahead, Cameli shares his low-maintenance curl routine, the styling tricks he’s picked up on set, what he imagines his Off Campus character’s haircare routine looks like, and the surprisingly simple essentials he never leaves home without. 

DashDividers_1_500x100

On his daily hair routine 

Like many curly folks, Cameli’s routine has evolved over the years. Where he once relied on strong-hold gels, he now reaches for products that leave his curls soft, touchable, and subtly defined. “I was more of a firm hold gel guy when I was younger, and now I just want something lightweight that’s not crunchy, and I can just enhance what I got going on upstairs already. But in my daily life now, I’m really just like a bedhead guy. I don’t want to put too much in my hair. I just want it to be light and easy, so the Defining Mousse is great for that.” 

DashDividers_1_500x100

On picking up beauty tips from set 

While his off-duty routine is relatively low-maintenance, Cameli admits he’s picked up more than a few tips and tricks from the on-set stylist. His biggest takeaway? “A diffuser goes a long way when you have curly hair. I don’t always use one at home, but when I’m preparing for work, a diffuser’s always a part of the process. It’s good to get a lightweight product like the Defining Cream from TRESemmé in first, since that will help you shape it when you go to diffuse. Also clips! When I want to look fancy, it’s good to go in with product and then clip your curls down and just let them air dry in a tight coil.” 

DashDividers_1_500x100

On Garrett Graham’s haircare routine 

If you were wondering whether Cameli has imagined what products his Off Campus character, Garrett Graham, reaches for, the answer is an emphatic yes. According to the actor, Garrett’s curls may look effortlessly tousled, but they’re definitely not accidental. 
 
“Garrett definitely has a hair routine because as you see, when he’s done playing hockey and his hair is really sweaty, his curls are falling in his face. Garrett’s a little more buttoned up on the day-to-day, so he does pull his hair out of his face a little bit more. Not completely, though — he’s not going in with any sort of gel, but he probably has a good lightweight curl product in combination with something with a little bit of hold. He’s probably using the Air Dry Foam to give it that hold after doing the lift.” 

DashDividers_1_500x100

On his self-care regimen

Cameli is the first to say that you don’t need an elaborate, expensive wellness routine to stay grounded and in the right mindset. Instead, he keeps it simple: move his body, spend time outside, and never underestimate the power of sleep. (Same!) “When it comes to my mental and physical health, the most important thing for me is exercise. You don’t even have to have a gym membership — going for a walk is a huge one for me, too. When it comes to at-home, I’m a big proponent of naps. I’m a big nap guy. People fight me on that a lot, but it’s crucial to getting through the day for me.” 

DashDividers_1_500x100

On his summer must-haves 

Forget the latest gadget or status bag. Cameli’s current MVPs are the kind of core staples that are life upgrades hiding in plain sight. “I can never resist a good pair of sweats, even when it’s really hot outside. I have a couple pairs of pants that I keep in rotation, and I wear all the time. Right now, I’m loving just a good pair of corded headphones for when I’m out and about or when I’m at work killing time. I’m just kind of cheap — I always forget my nice headphones. So I just go grab some corded headphones from the nearest store, and I keep one in my car, one at home, and one in my backpack so I can listen to music at all times. That’s a big one for me.”

title: The Ordinary’s $9 Caffeine Serum Made People Ask What I’d Changed
text:
The Ordinary’s $9 Caffeine Serum Made People Ask What I’d Changed

If you’re buying, mine’s a flat white with an extra shot and a dash of hazelnut syrup. And while I prefer to get my caffeine fix in coffee form, it seems I might be missing a trick when it comes to skincare.

This month, The Ordinary lifted the lid on its new Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum, which it calls an “energizing face serum to instantly refresh tired-looking skin.” As a longtime fan of all things The Ordinary, and who recently went through a stressful period that led to dullness, breakouts, and hyperpigmentation, it went straight into my bathroom cabinet.

Here’s everything you need to know about the new product and why it’s already racking up hundreds of five-star reviews.

The Ordinary Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum, $9

What is The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum, and what are the benefits?

According to The Ordinary, the latest addition to its burgeoning serum family firms, energizes, tones, and tightens skin. These are certainly bold claims, but the brand believes it can back them up with a handful of effective ingredients.

First up, caffeine. Consultant dermatologist Dr. Derrick Phillips tells me that while we’re often advised to limit the amount of caffeine we consume, applying it to the skin is a different story. “Caffeine is used in skincare for its antioxidant properties,” says Dr. Phillips, which helps protect skin against dulling environmental aggressors like pollution and UV.

There’s more. “Its ability to temporarily constrict blood vessels can help to reduce the appearance of puffiness, which is why it is commonly included in under-eye creams and serums,” adds Dr. Phillips. He explains that when applied topically, caffeine acts locally rather than having the whole-body stimulating effects associated with drinking coffee. That said, the results are generally temporary, explains Dr. Phillips: “It will all depend on the concentration of caffeine and the overall formulation of the product,” he says, “but it can be a useful ingredient for making the eye area look less puffy and more refreshed.”

Then there’s escin, not to be mistaken for ectoin, the moisturizing ingredient. I consider myself something of an ingredient know-it-all, but even I hadn’t heard of it before. Dr. Phillips says that escin, also known as aescin, is a mixture of naturally occurring compounds called triterpenoid saponins. “These are derived from horse chestnut seeds,” says Dr. Phillips, adding, “Escin has anti-inflammatory and anti-swelling properties, which is why it is sometimes included in skincare designed to soothe the skin and reduce the appearance of puffiness.” Escin could also provide similar antioxidant benefits to caffeine, but Dr. Phillips says that the research on its skin rewards is currently lacking.

Besides these two, there’s also dry skin-quenching glycerin — an ingredient I look out for in all my serums and moisturizers. Not only is it non-comedogenic, so less likely to clog pores and cause breakouts, but it’s also considered a humectant, so it draws much-needed moisture into the skin, making it smooth and plump.

What makes The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum special?

The multiple five-star reviews for The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum speak for themselves. One user says they wouldn’t be without the serum, while another praises its ability to make their skin appear more awake and energized. One simply refers to it as “age-reverse.”

Since incorporating it into my skincare routine over the last three weeks, I’ve been wearing much less foundation and concealer because I’m convinced my skin looks brighter, radiant, and more even in tone. Applying a full pump of CC cream has felt like a little too much for me, which I think is a testament to the 3% caffeine. Thanks to the high concentration of glycerin, my skin feels a lot more moisturized, too, and on some days, when it’s too hot for a full skincare routine, I just apply a generous amount of the serum.

I haven’t noticed any change in my facial structure, but serums in general can only do so much, and it seems Dr. Phillips agrees: “A topical serum may temporarily reduce puffiness and improve hydration, which can make the skin appear fresher, smoother and slightly more defined, but the effects of a serum are limited to the skin,” he tells me. It’s not all about your collagen, either, as Dr. Phillips explains: “Facial shape and structure are also influenced by the underlying muscles, ligaments, fat compartments, and facial skeleton, which a topical product cannot alter.”

That said, at a recent beauty event, an editor peer took one look at me and asked if I’d had work done. I hadn’t — just the serum — but when I asked what they were thinking, they said my skin looked smoother and glowing, sort of like a Botox effect. Interestingly, Dr. Phillips says that any immediate lifting or contouring effects like these from serums are likely temporary, thanks to a boost in the skin’s hydration levels or reduced puffiness. Still, I’m impressed.

What to know about The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum

• Contains 3% caffeine and 1% escin to boost hydration, radiance, and firmness, while bacillus ferment keeps skin strong and supple.

• Can help reduce morning puffiness when massaged into the skin for one to three minutes.

• Suitable for all skin types and can be used in the morning and evening.

How do you use The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum, and is it worth it?

I find that hydrating, milky serums like this work best when applied after cleansing (to dry skin) and before moisturizer or sunscreen. In the morning, I wash my face with a gentle cleanser (I like Dermalogica Magnetic[+] Afterglow Cleanser) and pat a pipette-full of the serum onto my skin. Once it’s absorbed, I wait a couple of minutes before applying my sunscreen — Thankyou Farmer Sun Project Light Sun Essence SPF 50+. Because this feels so replenishing, I tend to skip moisturizer altogether. In the evening, I double cleanse, apply the serum, and follow with Hada Labo Tokyo Plumping Gel Cream. A few nights a week, I swap the serum for retinal to exfoliate and keep my hormonal skin in check.

If you’re after an instant glow boost without the need for makeup, you won’t be disappointed by this serum. Who knows, people might even think you’ve had a tweakment here or there…

Where can you get The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum?

The Ordinary’s Caffeine 3% + Escin 1% Face Serum retails for $9 and is available at theordinary.com, ulta.com, and nordstrom.com.

title: I’ve Tested Hundreds Of Hair Oils — This Is The One I Always Recommend
text:
I’ve Tested Hundreds Of Hair Oils — This Is The One I Always Recommend

From clever hair growth tinctures to bond-repair treatments, the industry is bursting with innovative hair products that promise to stitch split ends back together, keep frizz on lockdown, and make hair appear impossibly glossy. But in my honest opinion, you can’t beat a simple hair oil.

Easily slotted into any haircare routine (whatever your hair type or texture), hair oils can be used on towel-dried hair to promote shine and boost moisture and manageability, or on dry hair to help with styling. There are plenty to choose from. Beauty brands love nourishing argan oil in particular, but castor oil, avocado oil, and coconut oil are just a handful that we can’t get enough of for promoting growth, softness and gloss. As a beauty director, I’m lucky to try hundreds of hair products which all pledge transformative properties. While there are so many brilliant buys out there, I always come back to hair oil, and there’s one product I will always suggest to friends, family or pretty much anyone who asks for my top hair recommendation: Kérastase Elixir Ultime.

What is Kérastase Elixir Ultime Hair Oil and what are the benefits?

Leave-in hair oil is nothing new. In fact, this particular hair oil has been a favorite for years. You might have spotted the iconic gold bottle on your hairdresser’s workstation or noticed boxes of the stuff stacked in your go-to salon’s window. Experts swear by it, and there’s a reason why it pops up everywhere: It really is as good as everyone says it is.

The star ingredients in the product are argania spinosa kernel oil (or argan oil), amodimethicone (a safe, hair-friendly silicone which leaves lengths ultra-soft, shiny, and frizz-free, and doubles up as heat protection), not to mention a megamix of other plant-based oils such as corn oil and marula oil, known for strengthening brittle hair strands.

What makes Kérastase Elixir Ultime Hair Oil special?

The texture feels more like a silky serum than an oil, which can be thick and sticky, separating hair or making it look greasy. As a result, it works across the board for all hair types, including fine hair. Experts say that argan oil, in particular, is one of the best oils for natural hair, improving elasticity and making strands soft. It’s especially great for curly hair, which tends to require more moisture. (There are some great YouTube reviews, too.)

My hair is thick, naturally wavy, and has been bleached and dyed multiple times over the past couple of years. Plus, I’m due a haircut, and I straighten my hair most days. It’s safe to say I need as much moisture as possible to minimize the appearance of split ends and my perpetually frizzy roots. I’m impatient, too, and anything that cuts styling time in half gets my vote. Elixir Ultime does all of that in just one tiny pump.

What to know about Kérastase Elixir Ultime Hair Oil

• A lightweight yet deeply moisturizing hair oil suitable for all hair textures.

• Formulated with a blend of nourishing plant-based oils and strand-friendly silicones for shine and heat protection.

• One pump goes a long way; it reduces frizz, adds shine, and comes in a refillable bottle.

How do you use Kérastase Elixir Ultime Hair Oil?

A pea-sized amount (raked through towel-dried hair and concentrated mainly on the ends) is all it takes to make my hair look like it has been professionally washed and styled, even if I’ve just given it a rough-dry and a very speedy once-over with my trusty ghd Chronos Hair Straightener. I can usually tell a product is excellent when I don’t use it. Testing shiny new launches means I often have to shelve Elixir Ultime for a couple of weeks at a time — and I notice a big difference in the quality of my hair.

While I don’t have any gripes, I have to acknowledge the price tag. At $62 for 75ml, this luxury oil is almost double the price of many hair oils the drugstore has to offer. That said, a little goes a very long way and the 100ml bottle is almost twice the size of some drugstore versions. Applied through damp lengths two to three times a week, mine lasts a good eight months, making it an investment beauty buy. The woody, musky smell also has me sold.

If you’re looking for cheaper alternatives with similar effects, Biolage All-In-One Multi-Benefit Styling Oil boasts Kérastase’s top ingredient: amodimethicone. Don’t let the complicated name put you off. While we’ve been made to fear silicones for clogging the scalp or “coating” hair, they are entirely safe to use, and it’s hard to deny how well they make hair gleam. As silicone transfers heat slowly, it also acts as a great heat protectant, shielding hair from blowdryers, straighteners, and curling wands. Silicones can easily be washed out with the right shampoo. This oil contains argan kernel oil, too, which moisturizes both hair and scalp and protects strands from environmental aggressors such as cold weather and pollution.

Also try Matrix Food For Soft Multi-Use Hair Oil Serum and Nexxus Repair & Nourish Ultra Lightweight Hair Oil. Both are R29 favorites with similar glossy hair ingredients.

Where can you get Kérastase Elixir Ultime Hair Oil?

Ultimately, though, not much truly beats my trusty Kérastase, which is available at Sephora and Amazon.

title: Lana Condor & Kathryn Newton Talk Representation, Their New Shark Movie & Body Positivity
text:
Lana Condor & Kathryn Newton Talk Representation, Their New Shark Movie & Body Positivity

Shark movies aren’t always looked upon fondly. But there’s a reason the genre continues to flourish: it’s entertaining, there’s room for strong female characters, and filmmakers can find a way to turn it on its head. In The Devil’s Mouth, director Jeff Wadlow explores themes of female friendship and growing up, while five friends fight for survival. One of the lead characters is Max, played by Lana Condor, a polarizing, confident sweet-talker. This isn’t the first Amazon-MGM thriller that Condor has played a lead role in — her action-ballerina film Pretty Lethal was released earlier this year — but that doesn’t mean Asian-American actors are being spoiled for choice.

“Within the past six years, we’ve seen more Asian representation, more leading roles, than we’ve ever [seen] before, but still, in comparison, [it] doesn’t even make a blip,” Condor tells Refinery29. “I definitely think more leading roles need to be written for us, because it’s really super easy to put us not in a lead.” Condor says it’s a “testament” to both The Devil’s Mouth and Amazon for championing non-white leads. “There’s work to be done, but there’s also a lot of us that are super stoked to do the work. So it’s really like, let’s get going,” she says.

Condor provided representation for East Asian women around the world when To All The Boys I’ve Loved Before was released in 2018, and she admits it’s something that has driven her whole career. “My honest-to-God reason that pushes me to keep making films [is that] I really want people to feel seen,” the actor says sincerely. “That’s what drives my basically, my entire want… I feel so grateful that I get to storytell just in general.”

The Devil’s Mouth also puts women in the spotlight. Condor’s character, Max, and Kathryn Newton’s character, Sara, are the beating heart of the film. Sarah Michelle Gellar previously said that only a few genres would allow women to lead early in her career. Horror has always been one of these, so it makes sense that The Devil’s Mouth continues that tradition. Newton is fast becoming a modern Scream Queen, after completing films such as Ready Or Not 2: Here I Come, Freaky, Paranormal Activity 4 and more, and she tells R29 genre films provide a special type of challenge.

“I love to entertain, and I think genre films reach a really wide audience. I think they’re challenging. I don’t think they’re easy. I think they’re hard to be convincing in, and [be] grounded and real,” the star says. “You know what’s going to happen in [The Devil’s Mouth]. It’s a shark movie. Someone’s going to die. Someone’s gonna get eaten, but how am I gonna keep you invested?”

The film relies on the actors to keep audiences invested, and the cast had to put their bodies on the line. “This movie had everything I thought I needed to be doing at the time. I wanted to be the lead of an action film, and I think Jeff Wadlow really helped me do that,” Newton explains. “You get banged up, but it’s all part of the fun. It adds to your performance… yeah, sometimes we were bleeding, but it didn’t slow you down. It was cool, it was cool to be bleeding. It’s like battle scars.”

There’s also body diversity in the cast, with Condor opting to wear a one-piece swimsuit while filming. She’s been open about healing from body dysmorphia, and was the topic of online chatter after going natural and braless for the Fashion Trust Awards earlier this year. While she’s not plus-sized, it’s still a relief to see curvier figures on screen, especially when extreme thinness is being celebrated in Hollywood at the moment. Condor says when she first received The Devil’s Mouth script, she had to think carefully about what it would entail.

“One of the first things that came into my brain was, ‘You will be very exposed. You are going to be in a swimsuit [for] three months in 4K’ or whatever it is,” she recalls. “When I was in fittings, I very much advocated for ‘I need to feel safe in my body, full stop.’ And I know this is a shark movie. I know that body is everything in a shark movie, because you’re swimming, and all you see is bodies in the water, I get it.”

The actor says it’s a vulnerable position to expose yourself under these types of conditions, so the costume team designed the one-piece swimsuit with specifications that would make Condor feel confident. “I’m curious to see the type of conversation that’s going to start [from this],” she notes. “I hope it’s a positive one, because it would be really hard if that was a topic of conversation in a negative way.”

With the way audiences embraced Ella Bright’s role as Hannah Wells in Off Campus, there’s a lesson for studios to learn here. We want more diversity. Whether that’s body size, gender, ethnicities, disabled or queer representation on screen, there are viewers waiting for it.

The Devil’s Mouth will be available to stream on Prime Video from July 29.
